chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others from both of them, peace be upon them, that they said:

Regarding the dog that a man sends and names (for hunting): They said, 'If you catch it and find its slaughter (throat) intact, slaughter it; and if you find it and it has already killed, and it ate from the prey, then eat what remains, and do not consider impure what they consider impure regarding the dog.'

key_terms.وَقَدْ قَتَلَهُ: And it has already killed it
key_terms.وَلاَ تَرَوْنَ مَا يَرَوْنَ فِي الْكَلْب: And do not consider impure what they consider impure regarding the dog
key_terms.يُرْسِلُهُ: He sends it (referring to the hunting dog)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of prey caught by a hunting dog halal if the dog eats some of it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of hunting with a trained dog, emphasizing that the prey remains halal provided the hunter recites Allah's name upon release. It specifically addresses the juristic debate regarding the dog's saliva and consumption, ruling that the remaining meat is permissible even if the dog has eaten part of it, thereby distinguishing this context from general impurity rulings. This reflects the Shia scholarly approach of differentiating between ritual impurity (*najis*) and culinary permissibility (*halal*) in practical scenarios.
